 John Mitchell: UFC Fighter Profile, MMA Record and Bio
 18 November 2026 by Mark Lawson 
 The Lowdown
 John Mitchell fights out of Cork, stands 6ft and arrives in the UFC Lightweight division with an 11-3 pro MMA record . Four of those wins came by knockout or TKO, two by submission and five on the scorecards. He is billed as “The Cork Horse” . Before the UFC call he fought for Cage Warriors and UAE Warriors, reached the PFL Europe final and won a 59-second title fight in Belfast. He is also 2-0 as a professional boxer.
 The River Before the Cage
 Mitchell was born in Cork city and came to sport through the water. His mother signed him up for rowing at 13 because there was a river close to home. He was good enough to race at the Junior European and World Championships, coached by Teddy O’Donovan, father of world champions and Olympic silver medallists Gary and Paul O’Donovan.
 He still credits rowing for his mental side. Halfway down a course, the body starts begging you to stop and you keep pulling anyway.
 Boxing came at 17. He had his first bout a month after walking into the gym and says he finished his amateur run as the top-rated fighter in Ireland and the UK. Then a trip to Thailand changed everything. He trained in Phuket and fought Muay Thai professionally there before he ever turned pro in MMA.
 His amateur MMA career brought belts at three weights, including three Cage Legacy Welterweight titles, Akuma gold at Lightweight and a Celtic Gladiator strap at Super Welterweight.
 The books got done too. Mitchell graduated from University College Cork with a BSc in Commerce in October 2019, a month before his pro debut, and then started an MSc in Sports Management at University College Dublin.
 First Leesider Ambitions
 He started out at MMA Cork, the McGuire brothers’ gym in Blackpool. Aaron McGuire ran his corner, and Craig Coakley at Dublin Combat Academy worked on his striking. From the start Mitchell had one plan, and he told the Echo he was determined to be the first Leesider in the UFC .
 He made his pro debut at Cage Warriors 110 at Neptune Stadium in his home city on 9 November 2019 and outpointed Eric Nolan. On 24 September 2020 he submitted Alan Brykalski with a rear-naked choke at 1:52 of the first round at Cage Warriors 114.
 Dubai and the First Scar
 After college Mitchell moved to Dubai, and it became home in most of the ways that count. He coached between his own morning and evening sessions and went straight into the UAE Warriors cage. A doctor’s stoppage of Arbi Emiev at UAE Warriors 20 and a decision over Konstantinos Ntelis at UAE Warriors 24 took him to 4-0.
 Then came Mariusz Mazur at UAE Warriors 28 on 26 March 2022. Mazur caught him in a guillotine and got the tap at 1:44 of the first round.
 Mitchell responded with stoppages. He finished Basel Shalaan in the third round at Sangai MMA Fight Night 2, then stopped Srikant Sekhar inside a round at Matrix Fight Night 11 in March 2023. PFL Europe signed him soon after.
 Berlin, Paris and the Night in Dublin
 The first PFL Europe lightweight tournament paid $100,000 to the winner. Mitchell beat Geysim Derouiche on all three cards in Berlin on 8 July 2023 and was furious with himself for not finishing him. When the bracket was reshuffled, he got Derouiche again in the Paris semi-final on 30 September and ground out another 30-27 sweep.
 The final was at the 3Arena in Dublin on 8 December 2023, against Polish kickboxer Jakub Kaszuba.
 Mitchell won the first round clearly. He hurt Kaszuba with clean shots, stuffed a takedown and even gave the Irish crowd a matador flourish. Kaszuba came out for the second round looking like a different fighter and stopped Mitchell with punches at 3:07 of the second round to take the belt and the cheque.
 Back to the Gulf
 He got back on track with a first-round rear-naked choke of Adham Mohamed at 971 Fighting Championship 1 on 4 May 2024. On 25 January 2025 he returned to the PFL in Dubai. Souhil Tairi went after a guillotine and more in the second round, but Mitchell got free, took top position back and won 30-27 on all three cards.
 The Makkasharip Zaynukov fight on 3 October 2025 still stings. Mitchell chopped at Zaynukov’s legs with kicks in the second round, but the judges gave the Russian a unanimous decision, and one card read 30-26. MMA News reported fans and commentators blasting the scoring as soon as it was read out.
 The Horsebox Gets Its Call
 The nickname has a story. His management first went with “The Ripper” after one bloody night, and it never fit. As he told The Irish News , “The Cork Horsebox” stuck instead, a nod to his strength and to rural Ireland. These days he is billed as The Cork Horse.
 On 4 July 2026 he headlined Cage Conflict 18 in Belfast in a title fight against Brazilian veteran Kallew dos Santos. He finished him with punches in 59 seconds.
 On 17 November 2026 the UFC signed Mitchell and Shoaib Yousaf for a late-notice bout at UFC Qatar . Mitchell is scheduled to face Shoaib Yousaf on 21 November 2026 at ABHA Arena in a Lightweight bout between two UFC debutants. Yousaf is an English former IMMAF world champion.
 Mitchell announced the news by crediting Fight Academy Ireland and called it “Gods Plan and History for Cork”, saying he is the first man from Munster to reach the UFC.
